LanguageData.CC_UI_Sub_Calendar: Days that matter to this colony, and how it keeps them.
LanguageData.CC_Cal_Intro: The days that matter to this colony, written down as its history happens: its founding, its first good harvest, the first snow, battles it remembers, people it lost, weddings, the arrivals of its first members and the birthdays of its long-serving colonists, the first child born here, the day the walls went up, a caravan home safe, the first harvest of a new crop, the first trade and a great hunt. When a day comes round, the colony can keep it with a feast, games, a rest day, a bonfire, a day of gifts, a hunt or a quiet hour. Kept {0} years running, a day becomes a tradition, and the colony expects it from then on.
LanguageData.CC_Cal_Off: The calendar's events are switched off in the settings. Days are still written down here, but nothing happens when they come round.
LanguageData.CC_Cal_NoCustoms: None yet. Answer a seasonal dilemma the same way two years running (a midsummer bonfire, a harvest home) and it becomes one of the colony's customs.
LanguageData.CC_Cal_Custom_Tip: A seasonal custom. It comes with the council's question about {0} each year, and the colony expects the answer it always gives.
LanguageData.CC_Cal_Pill_Kept_Tip: Years still to keep it before it becomes a tradition: {0}.

LanguageData.CC_Settings_Calendar_Tip: The days that matter to the colony (its founding, first harvest, first snow, battles, losses, weddings, the birthdays of its long-serving colonists, and days you name on the Calendar page) come round each year with a letter or a message, a feast, games, a rest day or a quiet hour.
